questions.prompt: In the movie "Interstellar," what is the name of the massive black hole?
questions.note: In the film, Gargantua is the supermassive black hole whose extreme gravity drives time dilation.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym ISRO stand for?
questions.note: ISRO is India's national space agency.

questions.prompt: What does the first "A" in NASA stand for?
questions.note: NASA expands to National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

questions.prompt: Which planet in our solar system is known as the "Red Planet"?
questions.note: Mars appears red because of iron oxide on its surface.

questions.prompt: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.note: Jupiter is the largest planet by both mass and volume.

questions.prompt: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.note: The Sun is our local star and by far the closest to Earth.

questions.prompt: Who was the first human to walk on the Moon?
questions.note: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon during Apollo 11 in 1969.

questions.prompt: In astronomy, a "light-year" is a unit of:
questions.note: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our Solar System?
questions.note: Our Solar System is in the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.prompt: In the movie "The Martian," which crop does the protagonist grow to survive?
questions.note: Mark Watney grows potatoes in the Hab to extend his food supply.

questions.prompt: Which celestial body was reclassified as a "dwarf planet" in 2006?
questions.note: In 2006, the IAU reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet.

questions.prompt: What fundamental force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.note: Gravity is the force that binds planets to their orbits.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is Earth's only natural satellite?
questions.note: Earth has one natural satellite: the Moon.

questions.prompt: What is the general shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun?
questions.note: Earth follows an ellipse with relatively low eccentricity.

questions.prompt: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is primarily operated by which agency?
questions.note: JWST is a joint mission led by NASA with ESA and CSA partners.
